Expiry's new sibling lookup uses the existing all-state message-key index. No new loop, timer, subscriber, poll or process-launch site was added in the F260 final-round delta. No performance regression blocks this head. D-F260-4 remains an accepted non-blocking follow-up, not a new gate.

Per-operation cost:
- Renewal: schema-version read, one queue BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, a jobs_serial(serial_key,state) scan of this recipient's failed history, then one primary-key UPDATE per selected hold. Its live-copy guard seeks jobs_dedupe_live(kind,dedupe_origin,dedupe_key), whose partial predicate excludes failed history; delivered ledger uses its unique recipient/origin/msg-id index. Returned payloads are still held until H outcome commits and the renewed-edge commit finish under the native lock. The corrected complete-edge transaction accounting is accurate.
- Expiry: schema-version read and one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction. The primary-key UPDATE terminalizes the named failed hold and returns four identity fields. If it returns no row (e.g. recovered body), commit and return false. Otherwise one additional SELECT checks the delivered unique index and jobs_by_dedupe(kind,dedupe_origin,dedupe_key). This is two application SQL statements inside one transaction, not one statement. It adds one in-transaction query/worker hop, not another pool acquisition or transaction.
- Sibling selection visits only copies of this kind/origin/key. Other recipients are excluded by the delivery kind established by the outer row guard. State/outcome/deadline and other.id exclusion remain residual predicates, so the all-state expiry index can visit this message's historical copies before deciding no eligible sibling exists.
- The existing sweep still walks parks from its24h window every60s (30s after failure, immediate replay after observed drops). D-F260-4 correctly records repeated no-op expiry transactions on already-recovered parks after their original deadline. Two hours is recovery eligibility, not deletion/retention.
